To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the perception of temporal diffuse reflection is a function of the ratio of the reverberation time of the room and the duration of the diffuse reflection, and that the perception of the diffuse reflection is independent of the duration of the direct sound.
a perceptually plausible simulation of room acoustics is possible for a wide range of rooms and that the simulation is computationally very efficient.

a single parameter can be derived from room geometry to quantify the perceptual relevance of temporal smearing in early reflections and that this parameter can be used to generate perceptually plausible room simulations for rooms which strongly deviate from a shoebox room.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the perception of sound in rooms, and how this perception can be reproduced by means of auralization. The focus is on
the design of auralized sound fields that are perceptually plausible.
the design of auralization algorithms that are able to generate perceptually convincing room acoustics for virtual reality applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RAZR approach provides an excellent compromise between accuracy and efficiency for room acoustics rendering in virtual reality.
the perception of early reflections is affected in the same way by temporal smearing of the diffuse part as it is affected by the shoebox room approximation.

the perceptual agreement of the proposed method is not significantly different from that of a state-of-the-art physical room acoustics model, while the computational complexity is significantly reduced.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we developed a new method for room acoustics modeling that is based on measured data, and is computationally efficient, perceptually plausible and applicable for auralization and virtual reality applications.
we developed a perceptual plausible room acoustical simulator which is able to simulate a wide range of room geometries.
RAZR is a fast and perceptually accurate room acoustics model for auralization and virtual reality applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the temporal smearing of the early reflections is perceived as an important feature for perceptually plausible room acoustic simulations, and that this can be achieved with the presented method.
perceptual plausible results can be generated for auralized stimuli as well as for the binaurally extended impulse response itself.
a perceptual agreement with natural room acoustics can be obtained by a simple temporal smearing of the early diffuse reflections.
